audit.whatIsWrong: Two of Mel’s abilities were attributed to the wrong slots, so the "bait this, then commit" advice pointed at the wrong spell.
audit.why: Solar Snare is her E, not her W; her W is Rebuttal. A player told to bait "W Solar Snare" watches the wrong cooldown and walks into the root anyway.
audit.corrected: Slot corrected in spikes[1], mid and wants.foe[1].

audit.whatIsWrong: The first-item and late spikes credited her ultimate with a damage reflect under a fabricated name, "Rewrite the Stars".
audit.why: Mel has no ability called Rewrite the Stars. The reflect is Rebuttal (W) and it is 38/35/33/29/26s. Her ultimate is Golden Eclipse (120/100/80s), which hits every Overwhelm-marked enemy at unlimited range and executes on enough stacks — a completely different threat, and the one that matters late.
audit.corrected: Fabricated name killed; spikes[2] now names Rebuttal, late now names Golden Eclipse and its real effect.

audit.whatIsWrong: Rebuttal was never mentioned at all, and the reflect it does have was attributed to her ultimate under a fabricated name.
audit.why: Riot's text: Rebuttal "forms a barrier around herself that reflects enemy projectiles back at the attacker, prevents her from taking damage, and grants her movement speed" on 38/35/33/29/26s. The part that decides an Aatrox commit is the damage prevention: a rotation dumped into an active Rebuttal does nothing, and a 38s rank-1 cooldown makes baiting it cheap for you and expensive for her.
audit.corrected: spikes[2] and mid now name Rebuttal, state that it blanks damage, and give the 38s.

edits.before: World Ender turns any trade into a kill; her W Solar Snare is her only peel, so bait it or dash through with E, then R and delete her.
edits.after: World Ender turns any trade into a kill; Solar Snare (E) is her only peel, so bait it or dash through with E, then R and delete her.

edits.before: After Eclipse you one-combo her — respect her R Rewrite the Stars reflecting your damage back, but her lane phase is already lost by now.
edits.after: After Eclipse you one-combo her — respect Rebuttal (W), a 38s barrier that blanks your damage outright, but her lane is already lost.

edits.before: Peel your engage with W Solar Snare root
edits.after: Peel your engage with the Solar Snare root

edits.before: From level 3 onward Aatrox owns this lane and the win[] reflects it. With your Q pattern plus E dash you close the gap she relies on, land the Q3 sweetspot knockup, and drain her down — she simply can't survive a committed all-in. At 6 World Ender's combat stats and heal amp make every trade a kill; her only answer is W Solar Snare to root you out of the combo, so bait it with a feint or dash through it with E, then R and finish. Keep the pressure relentless — she has no way to reset the lane.
edits.after: From level 3 onward Aatrox owns this lane and the win[] reflects it. With your Q pattern plus E dash you close the gap she relies on, land the Q3 sweetspot knockup, and drain her down — she can't survive a committed all-in. At 6 World Ender's combat stats and heal amp make every trade a kill; her answers are Solar Snare (E) to root you out of the combo and Rebuttal (W), a 38s barrier that stops her from taking any damage at all. Bait both, then commit.

edits.before: Your first item continues the beatdown — post-Eclipse you one-combo her — but the final phase evens back out. Mel becomes a real backline threat with high burst, a global R for map presence, and Rewrite the Stars reflecting your damage back at you if you dive carelessly. You can't reliably kill her through her team late, so cash in your massive early lead: take plates, roam, and close the game before her scaling makes her relevant.
edits.after: Your first item continues the beatdown — post-Eclipse you one-combo her — but the final phase evens back out. Mel becomes a real backline threat with high burst and Golden Eclipse (R), which strikes every Overwhelm-marked target at any distance and executes on enough Overwhelm stacks. You can't reliably kill her through her team late, so cash in your massive early lead: take plates, roam, and close the game out before her scaling ever makes her relevant.

edits.before: Snowball the lead before her scaling and reflect come online
edits.after: Snowball the lead before her scaling and Rebuttal come online

notes: MIRROR RECONCILED: the mel__aatrox audit states that Aatrox Infernal Chains is not reflected by Rebuttal — Riot describes W as a ground smash, and its derived "projectile" flag looks like a tooltip-parsing misfire. This file therefore claims only the damage prevention, which Riot states outright, and makes no reflect claim. Overwhelm (passive Searing Brilliance) executes on enough accumulated stacks, so late-game Mel threatens a threshold kill; not written to the page for space, flagged here. Aatrox's Infernal Chains (W) carries a derived "grounding" flag Riot's description does not support (drag + slow only); no grounding claim was made in this slice.
